items.title: A preliminary reassessment of Newton's alchemy
items.venue: The Cambridge Companion to Newton, 2nd edn
items.note: Reassesses Newton's alchemy in light of the digital edition and argues for its experimental, chymical character.

items.title: Newton the Alchemist: Science, Enigma, and the Quest for Nature's "Secret Fire"
items.note: Reads Newton's alchemy as laboratory chymistry built on decoding Starkey, Snyders and others, the interpretation any newly identified source will test.

items.title: newton_chymistry: rebuilt Chymistry of Isaac Newton website
items.note: Open code for the new edition site, generating pages and Solr search from the TEI encodings of Newton's alchemical manuscripts.

items.title: Encoding Newton's Alchemical Library: Integrating Traditional Bibliographic and Modern Computational Approaches
items.who: M. B. Mink, M. Dalmau, W. Hooper et al.
items.venue: Journal of the Text Encoding Initiative
items.note: Describes encoding the full corpus of over a million words and a bibliography of more than five thousand works Newton cited.

items.title: The Experimental Fire: Inventing English Alchemy, 1300–1700
items.note: History of English alchemy through the copying and reworking of manuscripts, especially the Ripley corpus, that Newton's generation inherited.

items.title: Theory and Practice in Newton's Alchemical Experimentation
items.note: First detailed comparison of Newton's alchemical theory with his laboratory notebooks, linking copied texts to his experiments.

items.title: The "chymistry" of Isaac Newton: a new Cu-acetate compound formed via crystallization
items.who: D. L. Bish, W. R. Newman and M. Pink
items.note: Replicates Newton's experiments with his 'vitriol' and verdigris and identifies the products by X-ray diffraction, showing his recipes can be tested in the laboratory.

items.title: A Bibliographical Framework for Citation Analysis of Isaac Newton's Alchemical Manuscripts
items.note: Revises the edition's citation encoding to allow terminus post quem dating of manuscripts and analysis of how Newton used sources.

items.title: EMLAP (Early Modern Latin Alchemical Prints), v1.0
items.note: Versioned release of a curated machine-readable corpus of Latin alchemical prints, usable as a comparison set for Newton's Latin copies.

items.title: An Alchemical Prima Materia for the Digital Age: Making the Early Modern Latin Alchemical Prints (EMLAP) Corpus
items.who: G. D. Hedesan, P. Pavlas and V. Kaše
items.note: Describes how the EMLAP corpus was built with Transkribus and human quality control, and its limits for comparative work.

items.title: Introduction: Computational Approaches to the Histories of Alchemy and Chemistry
items.who: F. Mahootian, S. A. Lang and G. Restrepo
items.note: Introduces an Ambix special issue on computational methods and sets out the evidential cautions needed when machines propose textual relationships.
